marker_line: Next SWC .27: .26 has identical TLS/switch code; fix false positives
verdict_basis: forager fetched .27 from npm with the requested SHA-256; it is byte-identical to the submitted archive. Both releases contain the expected addon, package.json, README.md and license.md, with no lifecycle scripts.

Fetched immediate predecessor 16.5.0-canary.26 (SHA-256 bc87a2329c0ac5bc4753e41096808d0ad28dedc6ac909d337bb15450fa6e23e1). All nonbinary content is identical except the manifest version. Both have 216 identical imports and 21 identical exports.

Both original addons have 31 TLS/relative-switch matches. All 31 instruction windows are byte-identical after zeroing RIP-relative displacements and relative call/jump destinations. TLS loads update allocation counters; enum tags from input objects select the subsequent SIB-indexed tables.

Meaningful added strings replace AvailableModules with AvailableChunkGroups, ChunkGroups and ChunkGroupWithIndex in Turbopack chunk/module-graph code; binary growth is 144384 bytes. This is ordinary compiler bookkeeping, not a new concealed dispatcher.

PE entry 0x184b9f4d0 initializes the CRT security cookie and enters normal runtime startup. TLS callbacks 0x184b0c380/390 initialize allocator state and handle thread teardown. napi_register_module_v1 at 0x1808e59d0 resolves Node-API entry points and constructs the exported JS interface.

The apparent game-query packet at file offset 0x55d8def is interior FF/55 data in the packed character-class table at VA 0x1855d9a80. Code at 0x18085a328 indexes this table, shifts by twice the low two codepoint bits and masks with 3. This is a two-bit property lookup, not a query request.

BrotliDecoderDecompress at 0x18005ea40 calls decoder 0x1800771d0, updates caller output length, and returns decoder success. Related exported stream and preallocated decoders plus brotli-decompressor source paths substantiate missing decompression coverage.

Decoded facts were reviewed: 8 XOR-stack candidates, 8 Base64 and 2 hex candidates do not supply scripts or a staged payload. Reviewed imports, startup, flagged dispatch and table-use paths agree with the published compiler purpose.
queue_premise: The immediate predecessor also fires the same suspicious trait under the current rules. The claimed clean predecessor does not reproduce as a release-code change.

changes.unsupported_claim: Nearby TLS counters plus ordinary indexed enum switches do not establish flattening.
changes.correction: Require a nonindexed ModRM pointer dereference after CMOV; retain minimum five and bounded TLS proximity. Describe proximity rather than asserting a TLS-to-target data flow. No product-name exclusion or severity reduction.

changes.unsupported_claim: A nine-byte initial challenge pattern inside a packed FF/55 lookup table does not identify a protocol record.
changes.correction: Require FF boundaries for the player record in PE/ELF read-only data. Preserve named query forms, exclusions, consumers and notable severity. Section start/end records remain recognized.
Add notable native decoder API symbol coverage; a string-only reference or decoder-state constructor is insufficient.

classifier.interpretation: No calibrated positive level before or after; module classifiers benign. Final YAML and analyst verdict agree. Installed model uses feature spec v18 and warns that v21 features are unavailable.

shared_rule_audit.tls_consumers: Reviewed all exact references: sideload, flattened remote-image injection, Defender/version-resource masquerade, unsigned loader, PRNG API-resolution, buffer encoding, erased-header and TLS reconstruction composites. Their true pointer-dispatch evidence is retained.
shared_rule_audit.game_consumers: Reviewed game-query-payload-forms, Perl DRDoS and IoT vector-set consumers. Existing query-flood-vectors.elf still matches the UDP observation, umbrella and suspicious DDoS vector set.
shared_rule_audit.controls: 15 generated PE/ELF operand/count/record-boundary/symbol controls passed; all 8 existing warp-query-review controls passed.

material_attack_detection_losses: None observed in the two recovered malicious loaders or existing query/DDoS fixture. Every other submitted-sample finding is preserved.
matcher_limits: The pointer-dispatch matcher covers unindexed memory operands; an indexed-only flattened dispatcher needs independently distinguishing evidence. Generic indexed dispatch and TLS observations remain notable.

Initial player packets merged into FF runs on either side are not recognized by this bounded-record alternative; named forms and source construction coverage remain. An isolated nine-byte pattern cannot prove network use.
missing_context: Static analysis only; the Windows addon was not executed. No installation/deployment context supplied. Judgment rests on inspected paths and exact registry/predecessor comparison, not clean scores or publisher claims alone.
